title: The wizard's write-nothing-before-every-prompt invariant now has an exception and nothing enforces which side a new prompt lands on
description:
Found during LCLI-466's implementation review, outside its acceptance criteria.

Before LCLI-466 the interactive wizard held a clean invariant, commented explicitly at the call site in src/commands/init.ts and attributed to LCLI-358.1: EVERY wizard question is asked before the first byte is written, so an EOF, a declined git prompt or a rejected flag combination leaves the directory exactly as the run found it, .git included.

LCLI-466 necessarily adds a prompt AFTER the base scaffold, because an id collision cannot be known until the migration actually runs. That is correct in this instance -- the migration is the write that failed, and Quest wrote nothing -- but the invariant's comment now describes a rule with one unstated exception, and nothing distinguishes a legitimate post-write prompt from an accidental one. The next person to add a prompt has no way to tell which side of the line they are on except by reading the comment and judging.

The task is to state the rule rather than leave it to a reader to notice: say what makes a post-write prompt legitimate (it recovers from a failure whose own write did not land), update the call-site comment so it stops asserting a universal it no longer has, and decide whether anything can enforce it -- a test that asserts the on-disk state at each prompt boundary is the obvious candidate. Prefer a check over a comment, per the fleet's standing preference for removing judgement over documenting it.

Related: the same 'put the exception in the claim, not two paragraphs down' problem the SDLC guidance calls out for prose, occurring here in a code comment.
